drivingQuestion: Does R' Yehuda refer to wood shavings or flax chaff?

segments.he: בִּנְסוֹרֶת שֶׁל חָרָשִׁין כּוּ׳. אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אַנְּסוֹרֶת שֶׁל חָרָשִׁין קָאֵי, אוֹ אַנְּעוֹרֶת שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן קָאֵי?
segments.en: We learned in the mishna: One may insulate food on Shabbat eve «in a carpenter’s wood-shavings,» and in the chaff of fine flax. Rabbi Yehuda prohibits doing so when it is fine, and permits doing so when it is coarse. «A dilemma was raised» before the Sages: Is the statement of «Rabbi Yehuda referring to the carpenter’s wood-shavings,» or is it «referring to the chaff of flax?»
